The issue is not tree_map. The problem is `x` that you are creating. If you do `jnp.ones(..., device=device)` that marks the output as committed which is why you see that error. Doing just `jnp.ones(...)` marks the output as uncommitted allowing JAX to move it to the devices of the context mesh.

See https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/faq.html#controlling-data-and-computation-placement-on-devices

Also note that you don't need to set the mesh globally. You can enter the mesh context in a scoped setting too via `with jax.set_mesh(mesh):` if you want to avoid these errors and only want the context mesh in a subset of your program.

timeline.body:
The issue is not tree_map. The problem is `x` that you are creating. If you do `jnp.ones(..., device=device)` that marks the output as committed which is why you see that error. Doing just `jnp.ones(...)` marks the output as uncommitted allowing JAX to move it to the devices of the context mesh.

See https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/faq.html#controlling-data-and-computation-placement-on-devices

Also note that you don't need to set the mesh globally. You can enter the mesh context in a scoped setting too via `with jax.set_mesh(mesh):` if you want to avoid these errors and only want the context mesh in a subset of your program.
